meta.title: One intake submission — extract, embed, retrieve, adjudicate, resolve

views.label: The path that runs
views.note: Three model calls, two deterministic steps, one outcome.

views.label: When no model answers
views.note: Both fallbacks end in a human looking, never in a silent merge.

messages.label: title + body, as written
messages.note: Untrusted from here on: validated by Zod, then only ever passed as data.

messages.label: insert the request, verbatim
messages.note: Before any model call, so a failure later cannot lose it.

messages.label: job, workaround, blocked outcome
messages.note: Degraded: with no recorded output the raw text becomes the statement and confidence is 0, which sends it to a human.

messages.label: 768-dim vector
messages.note: Degraded: an n-gram vector instead. It lives in a different space, so nothing in the corpus is comparable to it.

messages.label: ranked by cosine, no index
messages.note: One brute-force scan over all live problems. Candidates in another vector space are dropped and counted.

messages.label: one verdict + reason per candidate
messages.note: Degraded: every candidate comes back distinct. Nothing merges on a guess.

messages.label: 1 · same, score ≥ 0.80 → attach
messages.note: The verdict forms the attachment; 0.80 only decides whether a human confirms it. The demo request lands here at 0.822.

messages.label: 2 · same, under 0.80 → attach + flag
messages.note: needs_review = true. It is attached, and the review queue owes it a look.

messages.label: 3 · no same verdict → new problem
messages.note: Related candidates are recorded as links rather than being thrown away.

cards.title: What decides the outcome
items: The adjudicator's verdict decides identity. A same verdict forms the attachment; anything else creates a new problem.
The 0.80 threshold only decides whether a human confirms it, never whether the attach happens.
The score it is compared against is min(verdict confidence, cosine) — the weaker of two agreeing signals.

cards.title: Both degraded branches end with a person
items: No recorded extraction: the raw text stands in and confidence drops to 0, so the attach can never clear 0.80.
No recorded embedding: an n-gram vector, which shares no geometry with the corpus, so there is nothing to compare and the request becomes its own problem.
No recorded adjudication: every candidate returns distinct. A missing model never produces a merge.
Every one of those is labelled degraded in the UI rather than presented as a real match.

cards.title: What is not in this sequence
items: The request row is written before the first model call, so a failure later in the pipeline can never lose what the customer wrote.
Scoring. Factor estimates are a separate run (npm run score) over problems that already exist, so no band is computed here.
Nothing is queued or cached. Two model calls and one database scan happen inline, inside the request.
Every candidate considered is stored, including the ones that lost, which is what makes the offline threshold sweep exact.
